exercises.explanationUz:
MATNNING TO'LIQ NUSXASI:

  'The first thing you should remember when in
   England is always to say "please" and
   "thank you". Never push into a queue of
   people or they'll get angry. Don't be late
   for appointments and don't talk with your
   mouth full. Remember — always ask before
   smoking in someone's house.'


TO'LIQ TARJIMASI:
  'Angliyada eslab qolish kerak bo'lgan
   birinchi narsa — doim "iltimos" va
   "rahmat" deyish. Odamlar navbatiga hech
   qachon suqilib kirmang, aks holda ular
   jahli chiqadi. Uchrashuvlarga kechikmang
   va og'zingiz to'la turib gapirmang.
   Esda tuting — birovning uyida chekishdan
   oldin doim ruxsat so'rang.'


ANGLIYADAGI TO'RT QOIDA:
  1  Always say 'please' and 'thank you'.
  2  Never push into a queue.
  3  Don't be late for appointments.
  4  Don't talk with your mouth full.
  5  Always ask before smoking in someone's
     house.


RASM:
  Big Ben (Vestminster soati) va qizil
  ikki qavatli avtobus — Londonning eng mashhur
  ikki ramzi.


DIQQAT — 'A QUEUE':
  queue = navbat (odamlar qatori)
  O'qilishi: /kyu/ — faqat BIRINCHI harf
  o'qiladi, qolgan 'ueue' JIM!

  Britaniyada navbat — juda muhim madaniy
  qoida. 'to push into a queue' = navbatga
  suqilib kirmoq (juda qo'pol harakat).

  Amerikada 'a line' deyiladi.


DIQQAT — 'OR THEY'LL GET ANGRY':
  Bu yerdagi 'OR' = 'aks holda'.
     'Don't do it OR you'll be sorry.'
     (Buni qilmang, AKS HOLDA afsuslanasiz.)

  'they'll get angry' — WILL bilan natija
  bashorati (Unit 13 dan).
  'to GET angry' = jahli chiqmoq
  ('to BE angry' = jahli chiqqan bo'lmoq —
   holat, harakat emas).


DIQQAT — 'WITH YOUR MOUTH FULL':
  So'zma-so'z: 'og'zingiz to'la holda'.
  Bu — 'with + OT + SIFAT' qurilmasi:
     with your mouth full
     with your eyes closed
     with the door open


DIQQAT — 'THE FIRST THING ... IS TO SAY':
  'The first thing you should remember IS
   always TO SAY ...'
  Ega — 'the first thing', kesim — 'is',
  keyin TO-INFINITIVE.


YANGI SO'ZLAR:
  a queue          = navbat (o'qilishi /kyu/)
  to push into     = suqilib kirmoq
  to get angry     = jahli chiqmoq
  an appointment   = uchrashuv (belgilangan)
  with your mouth full = og'zi to'la holda
  to smoke         = chekmoq

points.en: The first thing you should remember when in England is always to say 'please' and 'thank you'.
points.uz: Angliyada eslab qolish kerak bo'lgan birinchi narsa — doim 'iltimos' va 'rahmat' deyish.
points.noteUz:
'when in England' — qisqartma
('when you are in England').

points.en: Never push into a queue of people or they'll get angry.
points.uz: Odamlar navbatiga hech qachon suqilib kirmang, aks holda ularning jahli chiqadi.

points.en: Don't be late for appointments and don't talk with your mouth full.
points.uz: Uchrashuvlarga kechikmang va og'zingiz to'la turib gapirmang.
points.noteUz:
'late FOR' — predlog 'for'.
'with your mouth full' — with + ot + sifat.

points.en: Remember — always ask before smoking in someone's house.
points.uz: Esda tuting — birovning uyida chekishdan oldin doim ruxsat so'rang.

exercises.explanationUz:
MATNNING TO'LIQ NUSXASI:

  'When in China, don't kiss anyone in public —
   it's very rude. Never be late for
   appointments, and don't tell jokes to people
   you don't know very well. Be careful when you
   are eating, too — never leave your chopsticks
   pointing upwards in your rice because this
   makes people very upset. A last tip — when
   you give someone a present, give it with both
   hands.'


TO'LIQ TARJIMASI:
  'Xitoyda odamlar oldida hech kimni
   o'pmang — bu juda qo'pol. Uchrashuvlarga
   hech qachon kechikmang va yaxshi
   tanimaydigan odamlarga hazil aytmang.
   Ovqatlanayotganda ham ehtiyot bo'ling —
   guruchingizga tayoqchalarni tik qilib
   sanchib qo'ymang, chunki bu odamlarni juda
   xafa qiladi. Oxirgi maslahat — birovga
   sovg'a berayotganingizda, uni IKKI QO'LLAB
   bering.'


XITOYDAGI BESH QOIDA:
  1  Don't kiss anyone in public.
  2  Never be late for appointments.
  3  Don't tell jokes to people you don't know
     well.
  4  Never leave your chopsticks pointing
     upwards in your rice.
  5  Give a present with both hands.


RASM:
  Pekindagi Taqiqlangan shahar (Gugong)
  darvozasi — an'anaviy xitoy me'morchiligi.


DIQQAT — TAYOQChALAR QOIDASI:
  'never leave your chopsticks pointing
   UPWARDS in your rice'

  Nega? Guruchga TIK sanchilgan tayoqchalar
  marhumlar uchun qo'yiladigan tutatqiga
  o'xshaydi — shuning uchun juda yomon belgi
  hisoblanadi.

  Matn buni 'this makes people very UPSET'
  deb tushuntiradi.


DIQQAT — 'MAKE + kishi + SIFAT':
  'This MAKES people very UPSET.'
  (Bu odamlarni juda xafa QILADI.)

  Qurilma:  make + [kim] + [sifat]
     It makes me happy.
     It made him angry.

  'to' YO'Q: 'makes people TO be upset' — XATO.


DIQQAT — 'TELL JOKES':
  'TELL a joke'  ✓  (hazil aytmoq)
  'SAY a joke'   ✗

  'tell' bilan keladiganlar:
     tell a joke, tell a story, tell a lie,
     tell the truth


DIQQAT — 'PEOPLE YOU DON'T KNOW VERY WELL':
  So'zma-so'z: 'siz yaxshi tanimaydigan odamlar'.
  Bu yerda 'who/that' TUShIRIB QOLDIRILGAN:
     people (WHO) you don't know very well
  Ergash gapda 'who' to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa,
  tushirib qoldirish mumkin.


DIQQAT — 'IN PUBLIC':
  'in public' = odamlar oldida, ochiqchasiga
  Artikl YO'Q — turg'un ibora.
  ('in the public' — boshqa ma'no)


YANGI SO'ZLAR:
  rude          = qo'pol, odobsiz
  in public     = odamlar oldida
  to tell jokes = hazil aytmoq
  chopsticks    = (xitoy) tayoqchalar
  upwards       = yuqoriga qarab
  upset         = xafa, ko'ngli buzilgan
  a present     = sovg'a
  with both hands = ikki qo'llab

points.en: When in China, don't kiss anyone in public — it's very rude.
points.uz: Xitoyda odamlar oldida hech kimni o'pmang — bu juda qo'pol.

points.en: Never be late for appointments, and don't tell jokes to people you don't know very well.
points.uz: Uchrashuvlarga hech qachon kechikmang va yaxshi tanimaydigan odamlarga hazil aytmang.
points.noteUz:
'TELL a joke' ('say a joke' XATO).
'people (WHO) you don't know' — 'who' tushgan.

points.en: Be careful when you are eating, too — never leave your chopsticks pointing upwards in your rice because this makes people very upset.
points.uz: Ovqatlanayotganda ham ehtiyot bo'ling — guruchingizga tayoqchalarni tik qilib qoldirmang, chunki bu odamlarni juda xafa qiladi.
points.noteUz:
'make + kishi + SIFAT' ('to' YO'Q).
Sababi: tik tayoqchalar marhumlar uchun
qo'yiladigan tutatqiga o'xshaydi.

points.en: A last tip — when you give someone a present, give it with both hands.
points.uz: Oxirgi maslahat — birovga sovg'a berayotganingizda, uni ikki qo'llab bering.

exercises.explanationUz:
MATNNING TO'LIQ NUSXASI:

  'When you visit someone in Japan, it is polite
   to take a gift. Remember to take your shoes
   off as you enter the house — they will give
   you special slippers to wear instead. Leave
   your shoes at the door, but make sure the
   toes are pointing towards the door. When you
   are in the living-room, don't sit anywhere
   you like — wait until someone shows you where
   to sit. Also, don't blow your nose in public —
   find a place where you can do it alone.'


TO'LIQ TARJIMASI:
  'Yaponiyada birovnikiga borganingizda,
   sovg'a olib borish odobdan. Uyga
   kirayotganingizda oyoq kiyimingizni yechishni
   unutmang — ular sizga o'rniga maxsus
   shippak berishadi. Oyoq kiyimingizni
   eshik oldida qoldiring, lekin uchlari
   ESHIKKA QARAB turganiga ishonch hosil
   qiling. Mehmonxonada bo'lganingizda,
   xohlagan joyingizga o'tirmang — kimdir
   sizga qayerga o'tirishni ko'rsatgunicha
   kuting. Yana, odamlar oldida burningizni
   qoqmang — buni yolg'iz qila oladigan joy
   toping.'


YAPONIYADAGI BESH QOIDA:
  1  Take a gift when you visit someone.
  2  Take your shoes off as you enter the house.
  3  Make sure the toes point towards the door.
  4  Don't sit anywhere you like — wait until
     someone shows you where to sit.
  5  Don't blow your nose in public.


RASM:
  An'anaviy kimono va soch bezaklaridagi
  yapon ayollari (geysha).


DIQQAT — OYOQ KIYIM QOIDASI:
  Yaponiyada uyga oyoq kiyimda kirilmaydi.
  Uy egasi SHIPPAK (slippers) beradi.
  Oyoq kiyimning UCHLARI eshikka qaratib
  qo'yiladi — chiqishda oson kiyish uchun.


DIQQAT — 'TAKE OFF' — AJRALADIGAN FE'L:
  'take your shoes OFF'  ✓
  'take OFF your shoes'  ✓
  Ikkalasi ham to'g'ri.

  LEKIN olmosh bilan FAQAT o'rtada:
     'take them OFF'      ✓
     'take OFF them'      ✗


DIQQAT — 'MAKE SURE':
  'MAKE SURE the toes are pointing ...'
  = ishonch hosil qiling, tekshiring

  Qurilma: make sure (that) + [to'liq gap]


DIQQAT — 'IT IS POLITE TO + fe'l':
  'It is POLITE TO TAKE a gift.'
  (Sovg'a olib borish odobdan.)

  Qurilma: It is + SIFAT + TO + fe'l
     It's rude to point at people.
     It's important to be on time.


DIQQAT — 'AS YOU ENTER':
  Bu yerdagi 'AS' = 'when' (payt).
     'as you enter the house'
     = uyga kirayotganingizda


DIQQAT — 'TO WEAR INSTEAD':
  'special slippers TO WEAR' — MAQSAD
  ('kiyish uchun maxsus shippak')
  'INSTEAD' = o'rniga (gap oxirida turadi)


DIQQAT — 'BLOW YOUR NOSE':
  'to blow your nose' = burnini qoqmoq
  (so'zma-so'z: 'burniga puflamoq')
  Yaponiyada bu odamlar oldida qo'pol
  hisoblanadi.


YANGI SO'ZLAR:
  polite        = odobli
  a gift        = sovg'a
  to take off   = yechmoq
  to enter      = kirmoq
  slippers      = shippak
  instead       = o'rniga
  to make sure  = ishonch hosil qilmoq
  a toe         = oyoq barmog'i; (kiyim) uchi
  towards       = ... tomon
  the living-room = mehmonxona
  to blow your nose = burnini qoqmoq
  alone         = yolg'iz

points.en: When you visit someone in Japan, it is polite to take a gift.
points.uz: Yaponiyada birovnikiga borganingizda, sovg'a olib borish odobdan.

points.en: Remember to take your shoes off as you enter the house — they will give you special slippers to wear instead.
points.uz: Uyga kirayotganingizda oyoq kiyimingizni yechishni unutmang — ular sizga o'rniga maxsus shippak berishadi.

points.en: Leave your shoes at the door, but make sure the toes are pointing towards the door.
points.uz: Oyoq kiyimingizni eshik oldida qoldiring, lekin uchlari eshikka qarab turganiga ishonch hosil qiling.
points.noteUz:
'make sure + gap'.
Sababi: chiqishda oson kiyish uchun.

points.en: When you are in the living-room, don't sit anywhere you like — wait until someone shows you where to sit.
points.uz: Mehmonxonada bo'lganingizda, xohlagan joyingizga o'tirmang — kimdir qayerga o'tirishni ko'rsatgunicha kuting.
points.noteUz:
'wait UNTIL' = ... gunicha kutmoq.
'where to sit' — savol so'zi + to-infinitive.

points.en: Also, don't blow your nose in public — find a place where you can do it alone.
points.uz: Yana, odamlar oldida burningizni qoqmang — buni yolg'iz qila oladigan joy toping.
points.noteUz:
'to blow your nose' = burnini qoqmoq.
'in public' — Xitoy matnida ham bor edi.

exercises.instructionEn: Listen and circle the correct word in italics.
exercises.instructionUz: Tinglang va kursiv so'zlardan to'g'risini aylantiring.
exercises.explanationUz:
BARCHA JAVOBLAR:
  1  ALWAYS
  2  LATE
  3  SHOES


HAR BIRI MATNDAN SO'ZMA-SO'Z TASDIQLANADI:

 1  'In England, ALWAYS/never ask before
     smoking in someone's house.'

    ANGLIYA matnining oxirgi gapi:
    'Remember — ALWAYS ask before smoking in
     someone's house.'
    → ALWAYS

 2  'In China, never be LATE/early for
     appointments.'

    XITOY matnidan:
    'NEVER BE LATE for appointments ...'
    → LATE

    DIQQAT: 'never be EARLY' mantiqan ham
    noto'g'ri — erta kelish hech qayerda
    taqiqlanmaydi.

 3  'In Japan, leave your gifts/SHOES at the
     door.'

    YAPONIYA matnidan:
    'LEAVE YOUR SHOES AT THE DOOR, but make
     sure the toes are pointing towards the
     door.'
    → SHOES

    DIQQAT: Yaponiya matnida sovg'a (gift) ham
    bor, lekin u eshik oldida QOLDIRILMAYDI —
    aksincha, uy egasiga BERILADI:
    'it is polite to TAKE a gift.'
    Kitob ataylab shu chalg'ituvchini bergan.


DEMAK AUDIO ShART EMAS:
  Kitobning o'zi 7b da aytadi:
  'Finally, READ THE TEXTS and CHECK YOUR
   ANSWERS.'
  Ya'ni matnlar javoblarni tasdiqlash uchun
  berilgan.

items.textEn: 1  In England, always/never ask before smoking in someone's house.
items.uz: Angliyada birovning uyida chekishdan oldin DOIM ruxsat so'rang.
items.whyUz:
ANGLIYA matnining oxirgi gapi so'zma-so'z:
'Remember — ALWAYS ask before smoking in
someone's house.'

'never' bo'lsa ma'no teskari bo'lardi:
'hech qachon so'ramang' — bu qo'pollik.

items.textEn: 2  In China, never be late/early for appointments.
items.whyUz:
XITOY matnidan so'zma-so'z:
'NEVER BE LATE for appointments ...'

'never be early' mantiqan ham noto'g'ri —
erta kelish hech qayerda taqiqlanmaydi.

DIQQAT: ANGLIYA matnida ham shu qoida bor:
'Don't be late for appointments.'
Shuning uchun 7b ning 10-bandi IKKI javobli.

items.textEn: 3  In Japan, leave your gifts/shoes at the door.
items.uz: Yaponiyada oyoq kiyimingizni eshik oldida qoldiring.
items.whyUz:
YAPONIYA matnidan so'zma-so'z:
'LEAVE YOUR SHOES AT THE DOOR, but make sure
the toes are pointing towards the door.'

DIQQAT — CHALG'ITUVCHI:
Yaponiya matnida sovg'a (gift) ham bor, lekin
u eshikda QOLDIRILMAYDI — uy egasiga BERILADI:
'it is polite to TAKE a gift.'

exercises.instructionEn: The statements from 1 to 12 are tips for visitors to England, China and Japan. Read the statements (1-12) and explain the words in bold, then guess which country each statement is for. Write J (for Japan), E (for England) or C (for China). Finally, read the texts and check your answers.
exercises.instructionUz: 1 dan 12 gacha bo'lgan gaplar — Angliya, Xitoy va Yaponiyaga boruvchilar uchun maslahatlar. Gaplarni o'qing, qalin harfdagi so'zlarni tushuntiring, so'ngra har biri qaysi mamlakat uchun ekanini toping. J (Yaponiya), E (Angliya) yoki C (Xitoy) deb yozing. Oxirida matnlarni o'qib, javoblaringizni tekshiring.
exercises.explanationUz:
BARCHA JAVOBLAR:

   1  E  (kitobda NAMUNA sifatida berilgan)
   2  J
   3  J
   4  C
   5  E
   6  J
   7  C
   8  E
   9  J
  10  E va C   (IKKI katakcha bor!)
  11  C
  12  E


MAMLAKATLAR BO'YIChA:

  ANGLIYA (E) — 5 ta:
     1  Ask before smoking in someone's house.
     5  Always say 'please' and 'thank you'.
     8  Never push into a queue of people.
    10  Don't be late for appointments.
    12  Don't talk with your mouth full.

  XITOY (C) — 4 ta:
     4  Don't kiss anyone in public.
     7  Never leave your chopsticks pointing
        upwards in your rice.
    10  Don't be late for appointments.
    11  Don't tell jokes to people you don't
        know well.

  YAPONIYA (J) — 4 ta:
     2  When you visit someone, take a gift
        with you.
     3  Take your shoes off as you enter the
        house.
     6  Don't blow your nose in public.
     9  Make sure the toes of your shoes are
        pointing towards the door.


DIQQAT — 10-BAND IKKI JAVOBLI:
  Kitobda 10-bandda IKKITA katakcha bosilgan:
     '10 Don't be late for appointments.
         ............., ............'

  Chunki bu qoida IKKI matnda ham bor:
     ANGLIYA: 'Don't be late for appointments'
     XITOY:   'Never be late for appointments'

  Javob: E va C.


DIQQAT — 'IN PUBLIC' IKKI MARTA:
  4-band: 'Don't KISS anyone in public.'  → C
  6-band: 'Don't BLOW YOUR NOSE in public.' → J

  Ikkalasida ham 'in public' bor, lekin
  HARAKAT boshqa. Faqat matnni o'qib ajratish
  mumkin:
     Xitoy matni — 'don't KISS anyone in public'
     Yaponiya matni — 'don't BLOW YOUR NOSE
                      in public'


QALIN HARFDAGI SO'ZLAR — TUShUNTIRISh:

  a GIFT = sovg'a
     'a present' bilan bir xil ma'no.

  TAKE YOUR SHOES OFF = oyoq kiyimni yechmoq
     'take off' — ajraladigan fe'l.

  to KISS = o'pmoq

  IN PUBLIC = odamlar oldida, ochiqchasiga
     Artikl YO'Q — turg'un ibora.

  BLOW YOUR NOSE = burnini qoqmoq
     So'zma-so'z: 'burniga puflamoq'.

  CHOPSTICKS POINTING UPWARDS
     = yuqoriga qaragan tayoqchalar
     chopsticks — xitoy/yapon ovqat tayoqchalari
     to point — ko'rsatmoq, qaramoq
     upwards — yuqoriga qarab

  to PUSH INTO A QUEUE = navbatga suqilib kirmoq
     queue — navbat (o'qilishi /kyu/)

  the TOES OF YOUR SHOES = oyoq kiyimning uchlari
     'a toe' — oyoq barmog'i; kiyimning uchi.

  an APPOINTMENT = belgilangan uchrashuv
     (shifokor, ish uchrashuvi va h.k.)
     Oddiy do'stona uchrashuv — 'a meeting'
     yoki 'a date'.

  a JOKE = hazil, latifa
     'TELL a joke' ('say a joke' XATO).

  MOUTH FULL = og'zi to'la
     'talk with your mouth full' — og'zi to'la
     turib gapirmoq.


QANDAY ANIQLANADI — KALIT SO'ZLAR:

   2  'gift'         → Yaponiya matnida
                       'it is polite to take a
                        gift'
   3  'shoes off'    → Yaponiya matnida
                       'take your shoes off'
   4  'kiss'         → Xitoy matnida
   5  'please/thank you' → Angliya matnida
   6  'blow your nose' → Yaponiya matnida
   7  'chopsticks'   → Xitoy matnida
   8  'queue'        → Angliya matnida
   9  'toes ... towards the door' → Yaponiya
  11  'jokes'        → Xitoy matnida
  12  'mouth full'   → Angliya matnida


DIQQAT — 2-BAND VA XITOY MATNI:
  Xitoy matnida ham sovg'a haqida bor:
  'when you give someone a PRESENT, give it
   with both hands.'

  LEKIN 2-band 'TAKE a gift WITH YOU' deydi —
  ya'ni sovg'ani OLIB BORISH haqida.
  Bu — Yaponiya matnining birinchi gapi:
  'it is polite to TAKE a gift'.

  Xitoy matni esa sovg'ani QANDAY berish
  haqida (ikki qo'llab), olib borish haqida
  emas.


MATNLARDA BOR, LEKIN 12 BANDGA KIRMAGAN
QOIDALAR:
  • XITOY: give a present with both hands
  • YAPONIYA: don't sit anywhere you like —
    wait until someone shows you where to sit
  Bular 8-mashqda ishlatilishi mumkin.

pairs.left: 1  Ask before smoking in someone's house.
pairs.whyUz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA.
ANGLIYA matnidan: 'Remember — always ask before
smoking in someone's house.'
'BEFORE + -ING' (before smokING).

pairs.left: 2  When you visit someone, take a gift with you.
pairs.leftUz: Birovnikiga borganingizda, o'zingiz bilan sovg'a olib boring.
pairs.whyUz:
YAPONIYA matnining BIRINCHI gapi:
'When you visit someone in Japan, it is polite
to TAKE A GIFT.'

DIQQAT: Xitoy matnida ham sovg'a bor, lekin u
sovg'ani QANDAY BERISH haqida ('with both
hands'), OLIB BORISH haqida emas.

GIFT = sovg'a ('a present' bilan bir xil).

pairs.left: 3  Take your shoes off as you enter the house.
pairs.whyUz:
YAPONIYA matnidan so'zma-so'z:
'Remember to TAKE YOUR SHOES OFF AS YOU ENTER
THE HOUSE.'

TAKE OFF — ajraladigan fe'l:
'take your shoes off' = 'take off your shoes'
Lekin olmosh bilan faqat: 'take them off'.

XITOY matnining BIRINCHI gapi:
'When in China, DON'T KISS ANYONE IN PUBLIC —
it's very rude.'

IN PUBLIC = odamlar oldida (artikl YO'Q).
DIQQAT: 6-bandda ham 'in public' bor, lekin
u YAPONIYA (burun qoqish).

ANGLIYA matnining BIRINCHI gapi:
'The first thing you should remember when in
England is ALWAYS TO SAY "PLEASE" AND
"THANK YOU".'

8-mashqdagi namuna ham shu:
'When in England, you should say "please" and
"thank you".'

pairs.left: 6  Don't blow your nose in public.
pairs.whyUz:
YAPONIYA matnining OXIRGI gapi:
'Also, DON'T BLOW YOUR NOSE IN PUBLIC — find a
place where you can do it alone.'

BLOW YOUR NOSE = burnini qoqmoq
(so'zma-so'z: burniga puflamoq).

DIQQAT: 4-bandda ham 'in public' bor, lekin
u XITOY (o'pish).

pairs.left: 7  Never leave your chopsticks pointing upwards in your rice.
pairs.whyUz:
XITOY matnidan so'zma-so'z:
'NEVER LEAVE YOUR CHOPSTICKS POINTING UPWARDS
IN YOUR RICE because this makes people very
upset.'

CHOPSTICKS = ovqat tayoqchalari
UPWARDS = yuqoriga qarab

Sababi: tik sanchilgan tayoqchalar marhumlar
uchun qo'yiladigan tutatqiga o'xshaydi.

pairs.left: 8  Never push into a queue of people.
pairs.leftUz: Odamlar navbatiga hech qachon suqilib kirmang.
pairs.whyUz:
ANGLIYA matnidan so'zma-so'z:
'NEVER PUSH INTO A QUEUE OF PEOPLE or they'll
get angry.'

QUEUE = navbat, o'qilishi /kyu/ —
faqat birinchi harf o'qiladi!
Amerikada 'a line'.

Britaniyada navbat — muhim madaniy qoida.

pairs.left: 9  Make sure the toes of your shoes are pointing towards the door.
pairs.leftUz: Oyoq kiyimingizning uchlari eshikka qarab turganiga ishonch hosil qiling.
pairs.whyUz:
YAPONIYA matnidan:
'Leave your shoes at the door, but MAKE SURE
THE TOES ARE POINTING TOWARDS THE DOOR.'

TOES OF YOUR SHOES = oyoq kiyimning uchlari
('a toe' — oyoq barmog'i; kiyimning uchi)
TOWARDS = ... tomon

Sababi: chiqishda oson kiyish uchun.

IKKI JAVOB — kitobda ham IKKITA katakcha
bosilgan!

ANGLIYA matnidan:
'DON'T BE LATE FOR APPOINTMENTS and don't talk
with your mouth full.'

XITOY matnidan:
'NEVER BE LATE FOR APPOINTMENTS, and don't tell
jokes ...'

APPOINTMENT = belgilangan uchrashuv
(shifokor, ish). Do'stona uchrashuv —
'a meeting' yoki 'a date'.

pairs.left: 11  Don't tell jokes to people you don't know well.
pairs.whyUz:
XITOY matnidan so'zma-so'z:
'... and DON'T TELL JOKES TO PEOPLE YOU DON'T
KNOW VERY WELL.'

TELL a JOKE ('SAY a joke' XATO).
'tell' bilan: a joke, a story, a lie,
the truth.

'people (WHO) you don't know' — 'who' tushirib
qoldirilgan.

pairs.left: 12  Don't talk with your mouth full.
pairs.whyUz:
ANGLIYA matnidan so'zma-so'z:
'... and DON'T TALK WITH YOUR MOUTH FULL.'

MOUTH FULL — 'with + OT + SIFAT' qurilmasi:
  with your mouth full
  with your eyes closed
  with the door open

exercises.instructionEn: What advice can you give to visitors to England, China and Japan? Give at least three pieces of advice for each country.
exercises.instructionUz: Angliya, Xitoy va Yaponiyaga boruvchilarga qanday maslahat bera olasiz? Har bir mamlakat uchun kamida uchta maslahat bering.
exercises.explanationUz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:
  'When in England, you SHOULD say "please" and
   "thank you".'

  QOLIP:
     When in [mamlakat], you should / shouldn't
     + [ASOSIY fe'l] + ...


ANGLIYA — BESH MASLAHAT:

  1  When in England, you SHOULD always say
     'please' and 'thank you'.
  2  You SHOULDN'T push into a queue of people,
     because they'll get angry.
  3  You SHOULDN'T be late for appointments.
  4  You SHOULDN'T talk with your mouth full.
  5  You SHOULD always ask before smoking in
     someone's house.


XITOY — BESH MASLAHAT:

  1  When in China, you SHOULDN'T kiss anyone in
     public, because it's very rude.
  2  You SHOULDN'T be late for appointments.
  3  You SHOULDN'T tell jokes to people you
     don't know very well.
  4  You SHOULDN'T leave your chopsticks
     pointing upwards in your rice.
  5  You SHOULD give a present with both hands.


YAPONIYA — BESH MASLAHAT:

  1  When in Japan, you SHOULD take a gift when
     you visit someone.
  2  You SHOULD take your shoes off as you enter
     the house.
  3  You SHOULD make sure the toes of your shoes
     are pointing towards the door.
  4  You SHOULDN'T sit anywhere you like — you
     should wait until someone shows you where
     to sit.
  5  You SHOULDN'T blow your nose in public.


BOShQA ShAKLLAR BILAN (99-betdan):

  WHY DON'T YOU ...?
     'Why don't you take a gift with you?'

  I THINK IT'S A GOOD IDEA TO ...
     'I think it's a good idea to say "please"
      and "thank you".'

  I DON'T THINK IT'S A GOOD IDEA TO ...
     'I don't think it's a good idea to kiss
      anyone in public in China.'

  BUYRUQ (matnlardagidek):
     'Always say "please" and "thank you".'
     'Never push into a queue.'


DIQQAT — 'ADVICE' SANALMAYDIGAN:
  Kitob ataylab 'three PIECES OF advice'
  deydi, 'three advices' emas!

     'an advice'      ✗
     'three advices'  ✗
     'a piece of advice'     ✓
     'three pieces of advice' ✓
     'some advice'    ✓

  Xuddi shunday sanalmaydigan otlar:
     information — a piece of information
     news        — a piece of news
     furniture   — a piece of furniture
     bread       — a piece of bread


DIQQAT — 'WHEN IN ENGLAND':
  Bu — qisqartma:
     'when (you are) in England'

  Ergash gapda ega 'you' va 'to be' fe'li
  tushirib qoldirilgan. Rasmiy va ixcham
  shakl.

  Xitoy matni ham shunday boshlanadi:
  'WHEN IN CHINA, don't kiss anyone ...'


YANGI SO'ZLAR:
  advice          = maslahat (SANALMAYDIGAN)
  a piece of advice = bitta maslahat
  a visitor       = mehmon, tashrif buyuruvchi
  at least        = kamida

points.en: When in England, you should say 'please' and 'thank you'.
points.uz: Angliyada 'iltimos' va 'rahmat' deyishingiz kerak.
points.noteUz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA.
'when in England' = 'when you are in England'.

points.en: When in England, you shouldn't push into a queue of people, because they'll get angry.
points.uz: Angliyada odamlar navbatiga suqilib kirmasligingiz kerak, chunki ularning jahli chiqadi.

points.en: When in England, you shouldn't be late for appointments or talk with your mouth full.
points.uz: Angliyada uchrashuvlarga kechikmasligingiz va og'zingiz to'la turib gapirmasligingiz kerak.

points.en: When in England, you should always ask before smoking in someone's house.
points.uz: Angliyada birovning uyida chekishdan oldin doim ruxsat so'rashingiz kerak.

points.en: When in China, you shouldn't kiss anyone in public, because it's very rude.
points.uz: Xitoyda odamlar oldida hech kimni o'pmasligingiz kerak, chunki bu juda qo'pol.

points.en: When in China, you shouldn't tell jokes to people you don't know very well.
points.uz: Xitoyda yaxshi tanimaydigan odamlarga hazil aytmasligingiz kerak.

points.en: When in China, you shouldn't leave your chopsticks pointing upwards in your rice, and you should give a present with both hands.
points.uz: Xitoyda tayoqchalarni guruchga tik qoldirmasligingiz kerak va sovg'ani ikki qo'llab berishingiz kerak.
points.noteUz:
XITOY — 4 va 5-maslahat birga.
Ikki qo'llab berish matnda bor, lekin 12 bandga
kirmagan.

points.en: When in Japan, you should take a gift when you visit someone.
points.uz: Yaponiyada birovnikiga borganingizda sovg'a olib borishingiz kerak.

points.en: When in Japan, you should take your shoes off as you enter the house and make sure the toes are pointing towards the door.
points.uz: Yaponiyada uyga kirayotganda oyoq kiyimingizni yechishingiz va uchlari eshikka qaraganiga ishonch hosil qilishingiz kerak.

points.en: When in Japan, you shouldn't sit anywhere you like — you should wait until someone shows you where to sit.
points.uz: Yaponiyada xohlagan joyingizga o'tirmasligingiz kerak — kimdir qayerga o'tirishni ko'rsatgunicha kutishingiz kerak.
points.noteUz:
YAPONIYA — 4-maslahat.
Matnda bor, lekin 12 bandga kirmagan.

points.en: When in Japan, you shouldn't blow your nose in public.
points.uz: Yaponiyada odamlar oldida burningizni qoqmasligingiz kerak.

points.en: Give at least three pieces of advice for each country.
points.uz: Har bir mamlakat uchun kamida uchta maslahat bering.
points.noteUz:
DIQQAT: 'three PIECES OF advice'.
'advice' SANALMAYDIGAN — 'three advices' XATO.

patterns.exampleEn: When in China, don't kiss anyone in public. When in England, you should say 'please' and 'thank you'.
patterns.exampleUz: Xitoyda odamlar oldida hech kimni o'pmang. Angliyada 'iltimos' va 'rahmat' deyishingiz kerak.
patterns.explanationUz:
'when in X' = 'when you are in X' —
ega va 'to be' tushirib qoldirilgan.
Ixcham va rasmiy shakl.

patterns.exampleEn: It is polite to take a gift. It's very rude to kiss anyone in public.
patterns.exampleUz: Sovg'a olib borish odobdan. Odamlar oldida o'pish juda qo'pol.
patterns.explanationUz:
Baholovchi qurilma.
'It is polite TAKING' — XATO.

'to' YO'Q: 'makes people TO be upset' XATO.
Shu kabi: It makes me happy.

patterns.exampleEn: Make sure the toes of your shoes are pointing towards the door.
patterns.exampleUz: Oyoq kiyimingiz uchlari eshikka qaraganiga ishonch hosil qiling.
patterns.explanationUz:
'make sure' dan keyin butun gap keladi.
'that' tushirib qoldirilishi mumkin.

patterns.exampleEn: Don't talk with your mouth full.
patterns.explanationUz:
Holat bildiruvchi qurilma:
with your mouth full, with your eyes closed,
with the door open.

patterns.exampleEn: Never push into a queue of people or they'll get angry.
patterns.exampleUz: Odamlar navbatiga suqilib kirmang, aks holda ularning jahli chiqadi.
patterns.explanationUz:
Bu yerdagi 'OR' = 'aks holda'.
Ikkinchi qismda WILL ishlatiladi.
